---
title: "How to read this course"
---

Every chapter is written in three layers, and you choose how deep to
go. Nothing in a deeper layer is required to follow the layer above it.

## The three layers

**Intuition first.** Each chapter opens with a few paragraphs of plain
prose, with no equations and no code. If you read only the openings and
the takeaway lists, you will still get the whole argument, e.g., why a
DCF has two free numbers, why persistent consumption risk carries a
price, and why value out-earns growth. Prerequisite: finance at the
level of knowing what a dividend, a return, and a price-earnings ratio
are.

**Derivations on demand.** The mathematics is in collapsible callouts
marked "Derivation". The callouts are closed by default. Open one when
you want to see where an equation comes from rather than take it on
faith. Prerequisite: comfort with expectations, logs, and the
stochastic discount factor, at the level of a first course in asset
pricing.

**Runnable code.** The code cell directly above each number prints it
at build time. Cells are folded where the code is routine setup, and
open where the chapter is explaining the code itself. Prerequisite:
enough Python to read a short script.

## What each part does

- **Part I: The puzzle.** The DCF's two free numbers, and the value
  premium as it appears in 74 years of data.
- **Part II: The toolkit.** The Euler equation, Epstein-Zin
  preferences, and the long-run risks consumption process, which are
  the pieces any general equilibrium valuation needs.
- **Part III: Solving the model.** A log-linear approximation you can
  read the economics from, and a quadrature grid that checks it.
- **Part IV: Testing against the data.** Calibrating cash flows without
  using returns, testing the market claim, and pricing the value
  premium.
- **Part V: Applying the model.** Price your own claim with the same
  steps, then read where the model misses and how far to trust it.

## How to run the code

Clone and install with `uv`:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/tlorans/kiku-value-premium-replication.git
cd kiku-value-premium-replication
uv pip install -e ".[fast,data]"
```

You can also work from a single chapter. Every chapter page offers a
notebook download under **Other Formats** at the top of the page. The
notebooks fetch the data files they need if you run them outside the
repository, so the only setup is the package itself:

```bash
pip install "lrrcs[fast] @ git+https://github.com/tlorans/kiku-value-premium-replication.git"
```

Details, extras, and the optional WRDS credentials are in
[Installation](reference/installation.qmd).

## The numbers policy

No number in the prose is typed in by hand. The code cell above each
figure, table, and in-text statistic prints it when the site is built,
and the prose is written to match the output, never the other way
around. Numbers that come from Kiku's paper rather than from the site's
code are always attributed as such ("Table IX reports…"). If a cell's
output and the surrounding prose ever disagree, the cell is right and
the prose is a bug, so please report it.
